faqs.q: Under Article 1 of the Constitution, the territory of India comprises how many categories?
faqs.e: These are territories of the states, union territories, and territories that may be acquired by the Government of India.

faqs.q: At present, how many union territories does India have?
faqs.e: They are Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Delhi, Lakshadweep, Puducherry, Chandigarh, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.

faqs.q: Union territories are also known by which alternative term, reflecting their direct control by the Centre?
In 1874, during British rule, certain areas were first constituted as what?
faqs.e: These were later renamed chief commissioners' provinces, and after independence placed in the category of Part 'C' States and Part 'D' Territories.

faqs.q: Which two enactments of 1956 constituted the 'union territories' as a category?

options.a: 65th Constitutional Amendment Act and the States Reorganisation Act
options.b: 7th Constitutional Amendment Act and the Government of India Act
options.c: States Reorganisation Act and the Union Territories Act
options.d: 7th Constitutional Amendment Act and the States Reorganisation Act

faqs.a: 7th Constitutional Amendment Act and the States Reorganisation Act

faqs.q:
Consider the following states, which were formerly union territories before being elevated to statehood:
(I) Himachal Pradesh
(II) Manipur
(III) Nagaland
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: Himachal Pradesh, Manipur, Tripura, Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh and Goa were formerly union territories; Nagaland was not.

faqs.q: In which year was the union territory of Puducherry created?
In which year was the union territory of Chandigarh created?
Till which year was Lakshadweep known by the name of Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi Islands?
Till which year was Puducherry known as Pondicherry?
Which union territory was created by merging Dadra and Nagar Haveli with Daman and Diu?

options.a: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

faqs.a: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
faqs.e: This merger took place in 2020; Dadra and Nagar Haveli was originally created as a separate union territory in 1961, and Daman and Diu in 1962.

faqs.q:
Consider the following pairs of union territories and the reasons stated for their creation:
(I) Delhi and Chandigarh – Political and administrative consideration
(II) Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep – Strategic importance
(III) Puducherry and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu – Cultural distinctiveness
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
In 2019, the erstwhile state of Jammu and Kashmir was bifurcated into which two union territories?
Which of the two union territories created from the erstwhile state of Jammu and Kashmir was designated to be without a legislature?

options.a: Both were designated without a legislature
options.b: Neither was designated without a legislature

faqs.q: Which Part of the Constitution contains Articles 239 to 241, dealing with the administration of union territories?
Every union territory is administered by the President acting through an administrator. In this capacity, an administrator is best described as what?

options.b: The constitutional head of state, like a governor
options.c: A representative of the Election Commission

faqs.q: At present, which of the following union territories has 'Administrator' (rather than 'Lieutenant Governor') as its designated executive head?
When the President appoints the governor of a state as the administrator of an adjoining union territory, in what capacity does the governor act with respect to that union territory?

options.a: On the advice of his/her council of ministers
options.b: Under the direct control of the Chief Minister
options.c: Independently of his/her council of ministers

faqs.a: Independently of his/her council of ministers

faqs.q: Which three union territories are provided with a legislative assembly and a council of ministers headed by a chief minister?

options.a: Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh and Delhi
options.c: Puducherry, Delhi and Jammu and Kashmir

faqs.a: Puducherry, Delhi and Jammu and Kashmir
faqs.e: Puducherry was the first to be given a legislative assembly, in 1963, followed by Delhi in 1992 and Jammu and Kashmir in 2019.

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the legislative power of Parliament over union territories with local legislatures:
(I) Parliament's power to legislate on State List subjects for these union territories remains unaffected even after a local legislature is established
(II) The legislative assembly of Puducherry can make laws on any subject of the State List and the Concurrent List
(III) The legislative assembly of Delhi can make laws on any subject of the State List, including public order, police and land
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: The Delhi assembly's law-making power over the State List excludes public order, police and land.

faqs.q: The legislative assembly of Jammu and Kashmir can make laws on any subject of the State List, except which two matters?
The President can make regulations for the peace, progress and good government of which of the following union territories?
In the case of Puducherry, when can the President legislate by making regulations?

options.a: Only when the assembly is suspended or dissolved
options.b: Never, since it has its own legislature
options.c: Only with the consent of the Chief Minister
options.d: At any time, regardless of the assembly's status

faqs.a: Only when the assembly is suspended or dissolved

faqs.q: Which union territory has had a High Court of its own since 1966?
Which High Court has jurisdiction over the union territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu?
Which High Court has jurisdiction over Chandigarh?
faqs.e: See table below for the administrative system of all eight union territories at a glance.

rows: Under Punjab and Haryana High Court
Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
Lt. Governor, Chief Minister, Council of Ministers
Lt. Governor, Chief Minister, Council of Ministers
Lt. Governor, Chief Minister, Council of Ministers
Under Jammu and Kashmir & Ladakh High Court
Under Jammu and Kashmir & Ladakh High Court

faqs.q: Which single high court has common jurisdiction over both the union territories of Jammu and Kashmir, and Ladakh?

options.c: Jammu and Kashmir & Ladakh High Court

faqs.a: Jammu and Kashmir & Ladakh High Court

faqs.q: Which constitutional amendment provided special status to the union territory of Delhi and redesignated it the National Capital Territory of Delhi?
faqs.e: This Act, which came into effect on 1 February 1992, also designated the administrator of Delhi as the Lieutenant Governor and created a legislative assembly and council of ministers for Delhi.

faqs.q: As per the 69th Amendment Act, what is the strength of the Delhi legislative assembly?
Elections to the Delhi legislative assembly are conducted by which body?
What is the strength of the Delhi council of ministers, fixed at ten per cent of the assembly's total strength?
faqs.e: This comprises one chief minister and six other ministers.

faqs.q: The Chief Minister of Delhi is appointed by whom?
Ministers other than the Chief Minister of Delhi are appointed by the President on whose advice?
In case of a difference of opinion between the Lieutenant Governor of Delhi and his/her ministers, to whom is the matter referred for decision?
The provision allowing the President to suspend the constitutional machinery of Delhi in case of its failure closely resembles which Article, dealing with President's Rule in the states?
Within how many weeks from the reassembly of the Delhi legislative assembly must an ordinance promulgated by the Lieutenant Governor be approved by the assembly?
Which ministry is the nodal ministry for all matters relating to union territories, including legislation, finance and the appointment of Lieutenant Governors and Administrators?

options.d: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

faqs.e: This is designated under the Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961.

faqs.q: How many union territories, being without a legislature, have the forum of the Home Minister's Advisory Committee or the Administrator's Advisory Committee?
faqs.e: These are Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Lakshadweep and Ladakh.

faqs.q: The Home Minister's Advisory Committee (HMAC) for union territories is chaired by whom?
Which Article of the Constitution provides for the power of the President to make regulations for certain union territories?
faqs.e: See table below for the range of Articles dealing with union territories and their subject matter.

rows: Creation of local Legislatures or Council of Ministers or both for certain Union territories
Special provisions with respect to Delhi
Provision in case of failure of constitutional machinery
Power of administrator to promulgate Ordinances during recess of Legislature
Power of President to make regulations for certain Union territories

faqs.q: Which Article of the Constitution, in Part X, envisages a special system of administration for scheduled areas and tribal areas?
The Fifth Schedule of the Constitution deals with the administration of scheduled areas and scheduled tribes in any state except which four states?
The Sixth Schedule of the Constitution deals with the administration of tribal areas in which four states?
The Fifth Schedule of the Constitution has been described by which phrase, reflecting its comprehensive framework for scheduled area administration?
Under the Fifth Schedule, who is empowered to declare an area to be a scheduled area?
faqs.e: The President exercises this power, including increasing or decreasing the area or altering boundaries, in consultation with the governor of the state concerned.

faqs.q:
Consider the following criteria for declaring an area as a scheduled area:
(I) Preponderance of tribal population
(II) A viable administrative entity such as a district, block or taluk
(III) Economic backwardness compared to neighbouring areas
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: These criteria for declaring scheduled areas are not spelt out in the Constitution itself, but have become well-established.

faqs.q: Regarding scheduled areas, the governor has a special responsibility to submit a report on their administration to whom?
Each state having scheduled areas must establish a body to advise on the welfare and advancement of the scheduled tribes. What is this body called?
How many members does a Tribes Advisory Council consist of?
faqs.e: Three-fourths of these members are to be representatives of the scheduled tribes in the state legislative assembly.

faqs.q: A Tribes Advisory Council can also be established in a state having scheduled tribes but not scheduled areas, if directed by whom?
Under the Fifth Schedule, who is empowered to direct that a particular Act of Parliament or the state legislature does not apply to a scheduled area, or applies with modifications?

Consider the following statements regarding regulations the Governor may make for scheduled areas under the Fifth Schedule:
(I) They may prohibit or restrict the transfer of land by or among members of the scheduled tribes
(II) They may regulate the business of money-lending in relation to the scheduled tribes
(III) They require the assent of the President
Which of the above is/are correct?
The Constitution requires the President to compulsorily appoint a commission to report on the administration of scheduled areas after how many years of the commencement of the Constitution?
Who chaired the first commission on the administration of scheduled areas and welfare of scheduled tribes, appointed in 1960?
faqs.e: This commission submitted its report in 1961.

faqs.q: Who chaired the second commission on the administration of scheduled areas, appointed in 2002?
faqs.e: This commission submitted its report in 2004.

faqs.q: How many states in India currently have Fifth Schedule Areas?
faqs.e: These are Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha and Rajasthan.

faqs.q: The special arrangements for tribal self-rule under the Sixth Schedule are confined to only four north-eastern states because many communities there had ruled themselves until being subjugated by which power in the 19th century?
At present, how many tribal areas exist across the four north-eastern states covered by the Sixth Schedule?
faqs.e: See table below for the tribal areas in each of the four states.

rows: North Cachar Hills District, Karbi Anglong District, Bodoland Territorial Areas District
Khasi Hills District, Jaintia Hills District, Garo Hills District
Chakma District, Mara District, Lai District

faqs.q: Under the Sixth Schedule, the tribal areas of the four north-eastern states have been constituted as what?
faqs.e: These autonomous districts do not fall outside the executive authority of the state concerned.

faqs.q: Under the Sixth Schedule, who is empowered to organise and re-organise the autonomous districts, including increasing or decreasing their areas?
Under the Sixth Schedule, if an autonomous district contains different tribes, the governor may divide it into what?
A district council under the Sixth Schedule consists of how many members?
faqs.e: Of these, four are nominated by the governor and the remaining 26 are elected on the basis of adult franchise.

faqs.q: Elected members of a district council under the Sixth Schedule hold office for what term, unless the council is dissolved earlier?
Nominated members of a district council under the Sixth Schedule hold office on what basis?

options.b: During the pleasure of the governor
options.d: During the pleasure of the President

faqs.a: During the pleasure of the governor

faqs.q:
Consider the following subjects on which a district or regional council under the Sixth Schedule may make laws:
(I) Land, forests and canal water
(II) Inheritance of property, marriage and divorce
(III) Levying income tax
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: All such laws made by district and regional councils require the assent of the governor.

faqs.q: Under the Sixth Schedule, whose consent is required for laws made by district and regional councils on specified matters like land, forests and social customs?
Under the Sixth Schedule, district and regional councils can constitute village councils or courts for the trial of suits and cases arising in what context?

options.a: Between the state and the Centre
options.d: Between the Governor and the council

faqs.q: Who specifies the jurisdiction of the high court over suits and cases handled by village councils or courts constituted under the Sixth Schedule?

options.c: The Chief Justice of the High Court

faqs.q: Under the Sixth Schedule, a district council may make regulations for the control of money lending and trading by which category of persons?
Under the Sixth Schedule, district and regional councils are empowered to assess and collect what?
Under the Sixth Schedule, on whose recommendation may the governor dissolve a district or regional council?

options.b: The recommendation of a commission appointed by the governor

faqs.a: The recommendation of a commission appointed by the governor

faqs.q: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the formation of an autonomous state comprising certain tribal areas in Assam?
faqs.e: See table below for the Articles related to scheduled and tribal areas.

rows: Administration of Scheduled Areas and Tribal Areas
Formation of an autonomous state comprising certain tribal areas in Assam and creation of local legislature or Council of Ministers or both therefore
Control of the Union over the administration of Scheduled Areas and the welfare of Scheduled Tribes

faqs.q: In whom does the power of direction over acts of Parliament or state legislature not applying to autonomous districts lie, in the specific case of Assam?

options.a: The President for Parliament acts, and the Governor for state legislature acts
options.b: The Governor for Parliament acts, and the President for state legislature acts
options.c: The President, for both Parliament and state legislature acts
options.d: The Governor, for both Parliament and state legislature acts

faqs.a: The Governor, for both Parliament and state legislature acts
faqs.e: In the case of Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram, this power lies with the President for acts of Parliament and with the Governor for acts of the state legislature.
